chapter: Dave Bartholomew band and early recording
title: Joining Dave Bartholomew's band
summary: Through Earl Palmer he joined Bartholomew's band, which played rhythm and blues, stock arrangements, carnival balls and out-of-town dances.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands

blocks.x: Not jumping too much. I guess we can sort of progress on to the Today Bartholomew Band. Was that the next big band? I mean the band that you played with? Real substantial organization that you joined, I would say.
And how did you get into Today?

Through Earl Palmer. He was with the Today Bartholomew's band. And when I joined the band, Frank Fields was in the band. Ernest McLean was in the band. Earl Palmer was in the band. Older gentleman by the name of Clarence Hall was playing tenor saxophone. And Joe Harris was playing alto. I'm trying to think of, there's a guy called P. Lou was playing piano. I'm not what his real name was. But that was the nickname, P. Lou. P. Lou. Yeah. Earl Palmer would probably, Dave would know what his real name was. And when I came in Dave's band, it was two tenors and alto trumpet.
Were you taking somebody's place? No. Somebody had been with the band? No. Okay. So tell me about Dave Bartholomew when you first joined the band.

What was? He taught you discipline. A variety of different kinds of styles. We would play dances at the San Jacinto and different other places. It all depends on what he called for. If there was a kind of a dance that wanted the rhythm and blues and what he did, we played that. And then we play formal things, where we played the stock arrangements of hit songs, you know.
And did Dave have a lot of that?
A lot of stock arrangements? Oh, yeah. Stock arrangements? Yeah. He needed that for, like, for instance, if he played balls and things like that.
Yeah, Dave did a lot of that, right? Yeah. And a lot for, say, social and pleasure clubs and the paternal organizations. Yeah.
Right. Right. And we would go in neighboring cities, you know, and play dances. And we did what Dave did, you know, rhythm and blues and whatever.
